direct_answer: Arthritis can affect the jaw joint and make chewing painful. If you are frail, eating less can quickly lead to weight and muscle loss. Softer, nourishing foods, smaller bites and jaw-friendly habits can help. See your GP or dentist if pain persists or you are losing weight.

content:
The jaw is a joint too. When it hurts, meals can become a struggle.

This guide covers eating well when chewing is painful. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

How jaw problems show up

  • Pain or aching around the jaw or ear.
  • Clicking or stiffness.
  • Difficulty opening the mouth wide.
  • Tiredness when chewing.

Eating enough when chewing hurts

  • Choose soft, moist foods such as fish, eggs, soups, stews, porridge and yoghurt.
  • Cut food into small pieces.
  • Add sauces and gravy.
  • Eat little and often.
  • Include protein at each meal.

Looking after your jaw

  • Avoid very chewy or hard foods.
  • Avoid wide yawning where possible.
  • Warmth may ease aching.

Getting help

See your GP or dentist for persistent jaw pain. Tell your GP if you are losing weight; they may refer you to a dietitian.

When to get help

  • Get urgent help if you have difficulty swallowing or breathing, or sudden severe jaw pain with chest pain (call 999).

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Is jaw pain always arthritis?

No. There are other causes, so get it checked.

Are nutritional drinks useful?

They can help if advised by a health professional.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Temporomandibular disorder (TMD)
  • NHS: Malnutrition
